Family / Category: Seated Core / Hip Flexor & Abdominal Strength
Alignment: Balanced on sit bones and tailbone; spine straight at 45°; legs straight or bent at 45°; arms parallel to floor.
Key Actions: Lift sternum; draw lower belly in and up; squeeze inner thighs; draw scapulae flat against back.
Safety / Contraindications: Acute lower back strain, tailbone trauma, pregnancy.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Bend knees with shins parallel to floor; hold backs of thighs; toes touching floor.
Benefits: Strengthens iliopsoas, rectus abdominis, transverse abdominis; builds mental focus.
Sequencing: Mid-practice core activation section; transitions between standing flows and floor work.
What Needs to be Opened: Hamstrings (if legs are straight), pectorals.
What Needs to be Engaged: Rectus abdominis, transversus abdominis, iliopsoas, quads, back extensors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Dandasana; Ardha Navasana (Low Boat), Hasta Padangusthasana C.
Common Misalignment: Rounding lumbar spine into a "C" curve; collapsing chest inward; splaying knees.

Family / Category: Seated External Hip Opener / Adductor Mobility
Alignment: Seated upright; knees bend out to sides; soles press together; heels draw to groin; hands hold feet; spine tall.
Key Actions: Ground sit bones; press outer edges of feet together; use outer glutes to draw knees down actively (no arm pushing).
Safety / Contraindications: Knee pathology (meniscus/ligaments), groin strains, acute SI joint dysfunction.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Sit high on blankets; blocks under outer knees for passive support; feet further forward (diamond).
Benefits: Increases adductor and groin mobility; improves pelvic circulation; prepares hips for meditation.
Sequencing: Transitional seated pose bridging standing external poses (Warrior 2) to seated folds and hip work.
What Needs to be Opened: Adductor magnus/longus/brevis, gracilis, pectineus.
What Needs to be Engaged: Gluteus medius, external hip rotators (gemelli, piriformis), deep core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Supta Baddha Konasana; Upavistha Konasana, Padmasana.
Common Misalignment: Yanking feet to crank knees down; slumping into lower back; sickling ankles.

Alignment: Prone; knees hip-width; knees bent, hands catch outer ankles; feet flexed or pointed.
Key Actions: Kick shins firmly into hands to lift chest; keep knees tracking hip-width (resist flaring); lift heart.
Safety / Contraindications: Hypertension, thoracic disc herniation, severe spondylolisthesis, pregnancy.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Strap around ankles; Half Bow (one leg at a time with opposite forearm down).
Benefits: Stretches front body (throat, chest, belly, groins, quads); strengthens back; stimulates digestion.
Sequencing: Mid-to-late backbending peak; follows Locust and Cobra; leads toward Camel or Wheel.
What Needs to be Opened: Psoas major, rectus femoris, pectoralis major, biceps, anterior deltoids.
What Needs to be Engaged: Hamstrings, gluteus maximus, spinal erectors, rhomboids.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Salabhasana; Natarajasana (standing Bow), Ustrasana.
Common Misalignment: Splaying knees wider than hips (jams SI joints); bending elbows instead of kicking; crunching neck.

Alignment: Supine; knees bent, feet flat hip-width, ankles under knees; arms along sides or hands interlaced under pelvis.
Key Actions: Root through feet; fire glutes/hamstrings to elevate pelvis; roll shoulders under; lift chin slightly off sternum.
Safety / Contraindications: Cervical disc injuries (never turn head while loaded), neck trauma, knee pain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Block under sacrum (Supported Bridge); block between thighs to prevent splaying.
Benefits: Strengthens glutes and hamstrings; stretches hip flexors and chest; calms nervous system.
Sequencing: First supine backbend in closing sequence; acts as diagnostic and prep for Full Wheel.
What Needs to be Opened: Rectus abdominis, iliopsoas, pectoralis major.
What Needs to be Engaged: Gluteus maximus, hamstrings, adductors, posterior deltoids.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Urdhva Dhanurasana (regressed blueprint); Eka Pada Setu Bandha.
Common Misalignment: Feet turning out like a duck; knees splaying wide; clenching outer glutes while losing adductors.

Family / Category: Kneeling Backbend / Hip Flexor & Thoracic Extension
Alignment: Kneeling with hips stacked over knees; shins/feet hip-width; spine arches back; hands on sacrum or heels.
Key Actions: Press shins down; push hips forward to stay stacked over knees; lift sternum skyward; wrap shoulders back.
Safety / Contraindications: Cervical spine pathologies (avoid dropping head blindly), knee pain, acute lumbar pain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Tuck toes to elevate heels; keep hands supporting sacrum; blocks outside ankles.
Benefits: Releases hip flexors and quads; expands lung capacity; mobilizes thoracic spine and throat.
Sequencing: Peak backbend or bridge to deep extension; must be followed by neutral spine transitions (Child's Pose).
What Needs to be Opened: Iliopsoas, rectus femoris, abdominal wall, pectorals, anterior neck.
What Needs to be Engaged: Gluteus maximus, hamstrings, erector spinae, adductor magnus.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Setu Bandha Sarvangasana; Urdhva Dhanurasana, Kapotasana.
Common Misalignment: Hips sliding back behind knees; crunching lumbar spine without thoracic lift; splaying knees wide.

Alignment: Kneeling; big toes touch, knees wide (or together); hips sink to heels; torso extends forward on mat; forehead rests down.
Key Actions: Melt chest toward floor; crawl fingertips forward to lengthen side waist, or arms along shins; breathe into back.
Safety / Contraindications: Knee pathology (avoid extreme flexion), ankle tightness, diarrhea.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Bolster lengthwise between thighs under torso; folded blanket between calves and buttocks.
Benefits: Releases lower back and hips; calms central nervous system; universal resting checkpoint in practice.
Sequencing: Opening grounding posture, transition between vigorous sequences, or counter-pose after inversions.
What Needs to be Opened: Gluteus maximus, thoracolumbar fascia, latissimus dorsi, anterior ankles.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Uttanasana (restorative kneeling); Uttana Shishosana (Puppy).
Common Misalignment: Hips lifting high into air without props; holding tension in neck and shoulders.

Alignment: Prone; legs hip-width, tops of feet grounded; hands under shoulders; elbows hugging ribs; crown extends forward and up.
Key Actions: Press pubic bone and feet down; peel chest up using back extensors without over-pushing hands; broaden collarbones.
Safety / Contraindications: Lumbar disc herniation, spinal stenosis, pregnancy, acute carpal tunnel.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Sphinx Pose on forearms; hands hovering an inch off mat; widen feet mat-width.
Benefits: Strengthens back extensors; opens anterior chest; stimulates viscera; counters kyphosis.
Sequencing: Early warmup in classical Surya Namaskar; regression before Upward Dog or Wheel.
What Needs to be Opened: Pectoralis major/minor, anterior deltoids, rectus abdominis.
What Needs to be Engaged: Erector spinae, rhomboids, infraspinatus, glute medius, core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Sphinx Pose; Urdhva Mukha Svanasana, Salabhasana.
Common Misalignment: Craning cervical spine; pressing all weight into hands; lifting pubic bone; flaring elbows.

Alignment: Supine; legs extended wider than hips, feet flopping open; arms alongside body 6–10 in away, palms up; spine neutral.
Key Actions: Consciously release all muscular tension; soften tongue from roof of mouth; release breath control; rest in stillness.
Safety / Contraindications: Late-stage pregnancy (recline on left side instead), severe acute lower back pain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Bolster beneath knees to flatten lumbar curve; folded blanket under head; eye pillow over eyes.
Benefits: Consolidates neuromuscular memory of practice; lowers cortisol and heart rate; restores homeostasis.
Sequencing: The mandatory final posture of every yoga practice.
Prep Postures: All preceding asanas serve as physical preparation for Savasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Whole body (systemic release of muscular tone).
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Tadasana (supine release); Supta Baddha Konasana, Yoga Nidra.
Common Misalignment: Fidgeting; skipping the posture entirely; forcing controlled breathing rather than natural respiration.

Family / Category: Seated Hip & Shoulder / Internal Rotation & Adduction
Alignment: Knees stacked on top of each other, feet beside opposite hips; one elbow points up behind head, opposite arm wraps behind back.
Key Actions: Root sit bones evenly; squeeze inner thighs; point top elbow skyward; keep head and neck upright.
Safety / Contraindications: Knee injuries (never force stacked knees), shoulder impingement, rotator cuff tears.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Sit on a block or blanket; keep bottom leg extended straight; use a strap between hands.
Benefits: Deeply stretches outer hip rotators and abductors (glute medius/piriformis); opens lats, triceps, pecs.
Sequencing: Late-sequence hip release; excellent counterbalance following wide external hip openers.
Prep Postures: Garudasana arms/legs, Baddha Konasana, Supta Gomukhasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Piriformis, gluteus medius, TFL, triceps (top arm), subscapularis/pecs (bottom arm).
What Needs to be Engaged: Deep pelvic floor, transverse abdominis, rhomboids.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Garudasana; Agnistambhasana.
Common Misalignment: One sit bone floating off floor; collapsing chest forward to clasp hands; craning neck forward.

Family / Category: Arm Balance / Scapular Protraction & Hip Flexion
Alignment: Hands shoulder-width; knees high on triceps/armpits; elbows bent (Crow) or straight (Crane); weight shifts forward to float feet.
Key Actions: Claw mat with fingers; protract shoulder blades (hollow chest); pull heels to glutes with hamstrings; gaze forward.
Safety / Contraindications: Carpal tunnel, wrist sprains, rotator cuff tears, pregnancy.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Feet on a block before lifting; block under forehead; lift one foot at a time.
Benefits: Builds wrist, forearm, shoulder strength; fires serratus anterior; trains core compression.
Sequencing: First arm balance introduced; transitional launchpad into Chaturanga or Handstand.
What Needs to be Opened: Wrist flexors, gluteus maximus, lower back extensors.
What Needs to be Engaged: Serratus anterior, transversus abdominis, rectus abdominis, psoas, triceps.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Malasana; Parsva Bakasana, Kakasana, Lolasana.
Common Misalignment: Looking straight down/backward (causes somersaulting); flaring elbows wide; jumping instead of leaning.

Alignment: Standing leg vertical; back leg bent, foot caught from inside or outside; torso hinges forward; back leg kicks back.
Key Actions: Kick back foot firmly into hand; square hips forward; lift sternum; stabilize standing knee.
Safety / Contraindications: SI joint instability, rotator cuff injury, knee ligament strain, low back impingement.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Yoga strap around back foot; hand on wall for balance; limit forward torso hinge.
Benefits: Develops balance and proprioception; expands anterior chest; strengthens back extensors.
Sequencing: Peak balance sequence; follows hip openers and backbends; leads to grounding folds.
What Needs to be Opened: Iliopsoas, rectus femoris, pectoralis major, anterior deltoid.
What Needs to be Engaged: Lifted leg glute/hamstring; spinal erectors; standing leg gluteus medius.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Dhanurasana; Virabhadrasana III, Standing Half Bow.
Common Misalignment: Splaying lifted hip open; flaring lifted knee outward; hyperextending standing knee.

Family / Category: Inversion / Deep Spinal Flexion & Sensory Withdrawal
Alignment: From Halasana, knees bend and rest on floor alongside ears; tops of feet flat; arms clasp on mat or wrap thighs.
Key Actions: Gently hug ears with knees; relax hips and spine into full flexion; maintain slow diaphragmatic breath.
Safety / Contraindications: Severe cervical issues, knee ligament injuries, acute sinus congestion.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Rest knees lightly on forehead rather than reaching floor; keep hands supporting back.
Benefits: Induces deep Pratyahara (sensory withdrawal); stretches neck and back muscles; calms anxiety.
Sequencing: Final stage of Shoulderstand/Plow sequence before rolling down into Fish Pose.
What Needs to be Opened: Entire vertebral column, glutes, hip rotators.
What Needs to be Engaged: Minimal active muscular force (passive surrender).
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Halasana; Balasana (inverted).
Common Misalignment: Forcing knees down into floor while straining neck; hyperventilating.

Family / Category: Inversion Prep / Scapular Stability & Hamstring Stretch
Alignment: Forearms parallel shoulder-width, elbows under shoulders; hips lifted in inverted "V"; head off floor; feet walk in.
Key Actions: Press forearms down; push floor away to elevate shoulders out of ears (protract/upwardly rotate); lift sit bones.
Safety / Contraindications: Shoulder impingement, rotator cuff tears, glaucoma, hypertension.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Interlace fingers; block between hands with strap around upper arms; bend knees.
Benefits: Builds shoulder/back strength without wrist strain; stretches posterior legs; preps Forearm Stand and Headstand.
Sequencing: Transitions from Plank or Down Dog; serves as prep for Pincha Mayurasana or Sirsasana.
Prep Postures: Adho Mukha Svanasana, Forearm Plank, Gomukhasana arms.
What Needs to be Opened: Latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major, posterior deltoid, hamstrings.
What Needs to be Engaged: Serratus anterior, middle/lower trapezius, triceps, core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Adho Mukha Svanasana; Pincha Mayurasana, Salamba Sirsasana.
Common Misalignment: Elbows splaying wider than shoulders; collapsing chest toward feet (sagging shoulders); head on floor.

Alignment: Inverted "V"; hands shoulder-width, fingers spread; feet hip-width; pelvis elevated; ears between upper arms.
Key Actions: Press index finger knuckles down; wrap triceps toward calves; lift sit bones high; press thighs back.
Safety / Contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome, late pregnancy, high eye pressure, wrist strain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Soften knees and elevate heels; hands on blocks or chair; widen feet to mat edges.
Benefits: Lengthens spine and posterior chain; builds shoulder stability; calms central nervous system.
Sequencing: Universal reset and bridge posture in almost every vinyasa sequence.
What Needs to be Opened: Hamstrings, calves, latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major.
What Needs to be Engaged: Serratus anterior, triceps, quadriceps, transverse abdominis.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Tadasana (inverted); Dolphin Pose, Three-Legged Dog.
Common Misalignment: Collapsing into wrists; rounding upper back; flaring elbows; hyperextending shoulders past ears.

Family / Category: Internal Balancing / Squeeze & Lateral Hip Stretch
Alignment: Standing leg bent; opposite thigh crosses high over standing thigh; toes point down or double-wrap; forearms bound.
Key Actions: Squeeze inner thighs and arms to midline; sink hips down; lift elbows to shoulder height.
Safety / Contraindications: Knee pathology (avoid forcing double-wrap); acute shoulder impingement.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Kickstand crossed toes on floor/block; bear hug arms (hands on shoulders).
Benefits: Stretches upper back (rhomboids/traps); releases outer hips and TFL; strengthens ankles and calves.
Sequencing: Peak of standing balances; compact counter-opening squeeze after wide hip-opening poses.
Prep Postures: Utkatasana, Gomukhasana arms, seated internal rotations.
What Needs to be Opened: Rhomboids, posterior deltoids, gluteus medius, piriformis.
What Needs to be Engaged: Adductor group (squeezing thighs), core stabilizers, standing quad.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Utkatasana; Gomukhasana, Seated Eagle.
Common Misalignment: Torso collapsing forward; twisting pelvis to force foot wrap; collapsing inner standing arch.

Family / Category: Lateral Arm Balance / Adductor & Rotational Integration
Alignment: Seated balance; hands framing hips; one leg slung high over shoulder; ankles crossed; legs clamp tricep as chest hinges forward.
Key Actions: Squeeze inner thighs and ankles tightly around arm; bend elbows 90° (Chaturanga arms); reach chest forward.
Safety / Contraindications: Wrist pathology, shoulder instability, inner groin pulls.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Practice seated Elephant's Trunk (Eka Hasta Bhujasana) to condition leg-over-shoulder without crossing.
Benefits: Strengthens wrists, arms, upper body; trains deep adductor and core compression; builds lateral control.
Sequencing: Peak arm balance; requires open hamstrings and warmed adductors; pairs with Side Crow or Compass Pose.
Prep Postures: Chaturanga Dandasana, Hasta Padangusthasana B, Navasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Hamstrings, external hip rotators (glute medius), wrist flexors.
What Needs to be Engaged: Adductor group, transversus abdominis, obliques, triceps, pecs.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Chaturanga Dandasana; Eka Hasta Bhujasana, Dwi Pada Sirsasana.
Common Misalignment: Letting bottom hip sink to floor; losing adductor squeeze on arm; dipping chest without extending legs.

Family / Category: External Standing / Lateral Extension & Hip Opener
Alignment: Stance 4–5 ft; front knee 90°; front forearm to thigh or hand to block outside foot; top arm extended diagonally over ear.
Key Actions: Press outer back foot down; wrap front hip under; spin lower ribs up; roll top chest open.
Safety / Contraindications: Meniscus tear in front knee, neck strain, hip impingement.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Forearm resting on front thigh; hand on high block outside foot; top hand on hip.
Benefits: Lengthens entire lateral body; strengthens thighs and ankles; increases hip mobility.
Sequencing: Partners with Warrior 2 and Triangle in lateral standing block.
Prep Postures: Virabhadrasana II, Utkatasana, Supta Baddha Konasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Adductors of both legs, intercostals, latissimus dorsi.
What Needs to be Engaged: Front quadricep, gluteus medius, obliques, back leg abductors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Virabhadrasana II; Utthita Trikonasana, Baddha Parsvakonasana.
Common Misalignment: Collapsing all weight onto front thigh/arm; top shoulder rolling forward; front knee knocking in.

Family / Category: Neutral Standing / Axial Flexion & Hip Hinge
Alignment: Feet together or hip-width; knees track over 2nd toes; hips sink back and down; torso parallel to shins; arms along ears.
Key Actions: Send sit bones back/down; press thighs toward midline; knit ribs; elevate sternum.
Safety / Contraindications: Acute knee injuries, meniscus tears, severe low back pain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Block between thighs; hands at heart (Anjali Mudra); back against wall.
Benefits: Builds heat; strengthens glutes, quads, calves; challenges ankle dorsiflexion.
Sequencing: Opening of Surya Namaskar B; transition into twists (Parivrtta Utkatasana).
What Needs to be Opened: Calves (gastrocnemius/soleus), latissimus dorsi, pecs.
What Needs to be Engaged: Quadriceps, gluteus medius/maximus, spinal erectors, core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Malasana; Utkatasana toe balance, Parivrtta Utkatasana.
Common Misalignment: Knees collapsing inward (valgus); knees shooting past toes; lumbar hyperextension.

Family / Category: Arm Balance / Deep Hamstring Flexibility & Core Lift
Alignment: Hands planted behind heels; thighs high on backs of upper arms; hips lift; legs extend straight out diagonally to sides.
Key Actions: Clamp inner thighs inward against arms; press floor away to round upper back; lift pelvic floor; drive through heels.
Safety / Contraindications: Hamstring avulsion/strains, wrist injuries, shoulder labrum tears.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Bhujapidasana (ankles crossed in front); keep knees bent over shoulders; hands on blocks.
Benefits: Dramatically increases hamstring flexibility; develops wrist/shoulder strength; builds pelvic floor lift.
Sequencing: Advanced peak balance following deep forward folds and adductor openers (Wide-Legged Fold).
What Needs to be Opened: Hamstrings, adductors, wrist flexors.
What Needs to be Engaged: Triceps, serratus anterior, iliopsoas, rectus abdominis, adductor magnus.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Kurmasana; Bhujapidasana, Astavakrasana.
Common Misalignment: Dropping hips toward floor; letting legs slip down elbows; collapsing chest backward.

Family / Category: Seated Hip Opener / Deep External Rotation
Alignment: Seated upright; shins stacked directly on top of each other parallel to front mat edge; top ankle on bottom knee; feet flexed.
Key Actions: Actively flex both feet to protect knees; sit evenly on sit bones; lengthen spine; hinge at hips for depth.
Safety / Contraindications: Meniscus damage or knee ligament instability (abort if knee feels sharp torque/pinch).
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Block or blanket in gap between top knee and bottom foot; cross shins loosely (Sukhasana).
Benefits: Isolates and releases deep external rotators (piriformis); mobilizes hip capsule; relieves lower back pain.
Sequencing: Peak seated hip opener; precedes forward folds and supine closing poses.
Prep Postures: Standing Figure 4, Baddha Konasana, Janu Sirsasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Piriformis, obturator internus, gluteus medius/minimus, IT band.
What Needs to be Engaged: Tibialis anterior (keeping feet flexed), core stabilizers.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Standing Figure 4; Eka Pada Rajakapotasana, Gomukhasana.
Common Misalignment: Sickling ankles; pulling feet too close to groin; rounding back instead of hinging pelvis.

Alignment: Supine; legs straight together; hands tucked under glutes palms-down; forearms press down to arch chest; crown touches mat.
Key Actions: Press elbows firmly down to elevate heart; slide scapulae down back; keep near-zero weight on crown.
Safety / Contraindications: Cervical spine pathologies, migraines, severe neck pain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Restorative Fish using two blocks (under thoracic spine and head); knees bent with feet flat.
Benefits: Expands rib cage; deepens breathing; stretches intercostals and throat; counters desk slouch.
Sequencing: Classical counter-pose following Shoulderstand (Sarvangasana) or Plow (Halasana).
Prep Postures: Bhujangasana, Setu Bandha Sarvangasana, Supta Virasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Pectoralis major/minor, intercostals, anterior neck (SCM, scalenes).
What Needs to be Engaged: Rhomboids, middle trapezius, erector spinae, triceps.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Bhujangasana; Supported Fish, Supta Matsyasana.
Common Misalignment: Dumping weight into cervical spine; lifting elbows off floor; holding breath.

Family / Category: Arm Balance / Deep Hip Opener & Core Compression
Alignment: Arm balance based on Figure 4; crossed front shin hooks across upper triceps, foot hooks outer arm; chest hinges forward, back leg flies.
Key Actions: Hook front toes around outer tricep; press shin into arms; lean chest far forward to float back leg; extend back leg straight.
Safety / Contraindications: Meniscus tears (torque on crossed knee), wrist sprains, rotator cuff strains.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Rest front foot on arms and lean weight forward without lifting back foot; block under forehead.
Benefits: Upper-body and core strengthener; deep release for outer hip and glutes; builds balance confidence.
Sequencing: Peak balance following Standing Figure 4 or Pigeon; requires open hips and Crow foundation.
Prep Postures: Eka Pada Utkatasana, Bakasana, Eka Pada Rajakapotasana, Chaturanga.
What Needs to be Opened: Piriformis, gluteus medius/maximus, hip capsule of crossed leg.
What Needs to be Engaged: Triceps, serratus anterior, deep core, back leg glute max and hamstring.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Bakasana; Eka Pada Utkatasana, Agnistambhasana.
Common Misalignment: Losing foot hook on outer arm; jumping back leg instead of leaning torso forward; flaring elbows.

Alignment: Forearms parallel shoulder-width; head lifted off floor gazing between forearms; body stacked vertically over shoulders.
Key Actions: Press forearms down firmly; actively lift out of shoulder joints; knit front ribs in; squeeze inner thighs.
Safety / Contraindications: Shoulder impingement, high blood pressure, cervical spine issues.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Practice at wall; strap around upper arms and block between hands; kick up one leg at a time.
Benefits: Strengthens upper back, shoulders, core; opens tight shoulders; builds balance and spatial awareness.
Sequencing: Peak inversion; follows deep shoulder openers (Dolphin, Gomukhasana) and precedes floor cooldown.
Prep Postures: Dolphin Pose, Forearm Plank, Adho Mukha Svanasana, Gomukhasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major/minor, subscapularis.
What Needs to be Engaged: Serratus anterior, deltoids, triceps, transverse abdominis, erectors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Dolphin Pose; Adho Mukha Vrksasana, Vrischikasana (Scorpion).
Common Misalignment: Flaring elbows wide; sinking into shoulders; banana-back arching due to tight shoulders.

Family / Category: Neutral Prone / Arm Balance & Core Stabilization
Alignment: Body in one rigid plane; elbows bent at 90° stacked over wrists; upper arms parallel to floor; shoulders away from ears.
Key Actions: Reach heels back while pulling chest forward; wrap triceps back; knit anterior core and ribs.
Safety / Contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome, shoulder impingement, labrum tears, wrist injury.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Lower knees to floor; block under sternum; practice against wall.
Benefits: Builds upper-body and core stability; preps shoulders/wrists for arm balances.
Sequencing: Primary transition between High Plank and Upward Dog in vinyasa flows.
What Needs to be Opened: Anterior chest, forearm flexors, wrist extensors.
What Needs to be Engaged: Triceps, serratus anterior, pectorals, transverse abdominis, quads.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Phalakasana; Ashtanga Namaskara, Upward Plank.
Common Misalignment: Shoulders dumping forward below elbows; sagging hips; flaring elbows outward.

Alignment: Feet parallel; torso parallel to floor; spine elongated from tailbone to crown; hands on floor, blocks, or shins.
Key Actions: Reach sternum forward; press shoulder blades onto back ribs; tilt sit bones up; firm core.
Safety / Contraindications: Cervical strain (avoid craning neck), acute hamstring tears, disc injuries.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hands on blocks under shoulders; hands on shins/thighs; soft knees.
Benefits: Strengthens back extensors; stretches proximal hamstrings; reinforces neutral spine mechanics.
Sequencing: Reset transition between Uttanasana and Chaturanga in Surya Namaskar.
What Needs to be Opened: Proximal hamstrings, calf complex.
What Needs to be Engaged: Erector spinae, rhomboids, serratus anterior, quads.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Dandasana; Virabhadrasana III, Ardha Chandrasana (torso alignment).
Common Misalignment: Kyphotic thoracic rounding; hyperextending cervical spine; locking knees.

Alignment: Bottom leg bent with heel outside opposite hip; top leg crossed with foot flat; torso twists to top knee; elbow hooks knee.
Key Actions: Anchor both sit bones; inhale to lengthen spine tall; exhale to twist from rib cage; head turns last.
Safety / Contraindications: Herniated lumbar discs, SI joint dysfunction, pregnancy.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Keep bottom leg extended straight; hug knee with forearm instead of hooking elbow.
Benefits: Mobilizes thoracic spine; massages abdominal organs; stretches outer hips and piriformis.
Sequencing: Counter-pose and neutralizer following deep forward folds or backbends; preps cooldown.
What Needs to be Opened: Thoracic spine, piriformis, gluteus medius, pectorals.
What Needs to be Engaged: Internal and external obliques, transverse abdominis, spinal erectors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Dandasana; Marichyasana III, Parivrtta Utkatasana.
Common Misalignment: Lifting top sit bone off floor; slumping backward onto back hand; cranking neck to twist.

Alignment: Standing leg grounded; bottom hand 8–12 in ahead/outside pinky toe; top leg, hip, chest stacked laterally.
Key Actions: Stack top hip over bottom hip; flex top foot with toes pointing sideways; press through bottom foot; expand arms.
Safety / Contraindications: Sacroiliac instability, inner ear issues, acute neck injuries.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hand on block at highest height; soft standing knee; back against wall.
Benefits: Strengthens standing ankle and glute medius; improves balance and lateral core; opens chest and groins.
Sequencing: Late standing sequence; unfolds from Warrior 2 or Triangle; leads into Chapasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Adductors of both legs, standing hamstring, pectorals.
What Needs to be Engaged: Gluteus medius and TFL (both legs), quads, lateral obliques.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Utthita Trikonasana; Chapasana, Parivrtta Ardha Chandrasana.
Common Misalignment: Bottom hand placed too close to foot; top hip rolling down; lifted leg sagging below hip height.

Alignment: Standing leg straight; lifted leg extended forward at hip height; two-finger grip on big toe; hips level.
Key Actions: Ground standing foot; pull lifted femur back into socket; engage core; draw reaching shoulder back.
Safety / Contraindications: Hamstring origin tears, lower back disc injuries, acute ankle sprains.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hold bent knee with hand; strap around ball of foot; lean back against wall.

Key Actions: Press forearms down with 85–90% of weight (light head contact); knit ribs; squeeze inner legs; flex/point feet.
Safety / Contraindications: Cervical spine pathologies (herniations, arthritis), glaucoma, detached retina, hypertension.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Practice at a wall; Dolphin Pose (head off floor); practice using inversion chairs/props.
Benefits: Enhances venous return to heart; increases focus; builds shoulder girdle and deep core stability.
Sequencing: Calming inversion placed near end of active sequence; must be followed by Child's Pose.
Prep Postures: Dolphin Pose, Forearm Plank, Prasarita Padottanasana, Navasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Latissimus dorsi, hamstrings (for pike entry).
What Needs to be Engaged: Serratus anterior, trapezius, rectus/transverse abdominis, adductors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Tadasana (inverted); Sirsasana II (Tripod), Pincha Mayurasana.
Common Misalignment: Dumping body weight into cervical vertebrae; elbows splaying wide; banana-back lumbar arching.

Alignment: Inverted; weight on tops of shoulders and upper arms (never cervical neck); hands support back; legs vertical.
Key Actions: Walk elbows closer behind back; press upper arms down; lift chest toward chin (do not turn head); reach toes up.
Safety / Contraindications: Cervical pathologies, disc herniations, high blood pressure, glaucoma.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Folded blankets beneath shoulders to leave neck free; Legs-Up-the-Wall; Supported Bridge on block.
Benefits: Stimulates baroreceptors (lowers heart rate/BP); soothes nervous system; drains venous blood from legs.
Sequencing: Classical cooling inversion at end of practice; followed by Halasana and counter-posed by Fish Pose.
What Needs to be Opened: Posterior cervical spine, upper trapezius, hamstrings.
What Needs to be Engaged: Triceps, posterior deltoids, rhomboids, transverse abdominis, adductors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Setu Bandha Sarvangasana; Halasana, Karnapidasana.
Common Misalignment: Elbows splaying wide (dumping weight onto neck); turning head side-to-side; hips sagging backward.

Family / Category: External Standing Balance / Asymmetrical Hip Opener
Alignment: Standing leg vertical; opposite foot pressed to inner ankle, calf, or inner upper thigh (never knee); pelvis square.
Key Actions: Oppose foot and inner leg pressure; externally rotate bent knee; ground through big toe mound.
Safety / Contraindications: Knee pathology (avoid placing foot on knee joint); vertigo/balance issues.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Kickstand foot at ankle with toes on floor; hands at heart; hold wall.
Benefits: Strengthens ankles, calves, pelvic stabilizers; improves proprioception; gently opens hip rotators.
Sequencing: First standing balance introduced; establishes stability before advancing to dynamic balances.
Prep Postures: Tadasana, Baddha Konasana, Supta Padangusthasana B.
What Needs to be Opened: Hip adductors, psoas, external hip rotators.
What Needs to be Engaged: Standing gluteus medius and quads; deep core stabilizers.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Tadasana; Utthita Hasta Padangusthasana B, Padmasana preps.
Common Misalignment: Placing foot directly on lateral knee joint; popping hip outward; rotating hips toward knee.

Family / Category: External Standing / Lateral Extension & Hamstring Stretch
Alignment: Stance 3.5–4.5 ft; both legs straight; front foot forward, back foot turned in 60–75°; spine extended laterally over front leg.
Key Actions: Wrap front thigh outward; tuck front sit bone under; reach front arm far forward before lowering hand; stack shoulders.
Safety / Contraindications: Hamstring insertion strain, SI joint irritation, cervical neck injury.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hand on block outside front shin; micro-bend front knee; top hand resting on hip.
Benefits: Stretches hamstrings, adductors, lateral spine; opens chest; builds lateral core strength.
Sequencing: Follows Warrior 2; natural transition toward Half Moon or Wide-Legged Fold.
Prep Postures: Virabhadrasana II, Supta Padangusthasana B, Prasarita Padottanasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Hamstrings of front leg, adductor longus, thoracic chest cavity.
What Needs to be Engaged: Quadriceps (reciprocal inhibition), obliques, gluteus medius.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Utthita Parsvakonasana; Parivrtta Trikonasana, Ardha Chandrasana.
Common Misalignment: Hyperextending front knee; collapsing lower ribs and hunching chest forward; hip jutting back.

Alignment: Supine; feet flat hip-width; hands by ears with fingers toward shoulders; press up to extend arms fully.
Key Actions: Ground inner feet; roll inner thighs down; push chest through upper arms; rotate upper arms externally.
Safety / Contraindications: Wrist impingement, rotator cuff tears, lumbar facet syndrome, hypertension, glaucoma.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hands on blocks against wall; strap around upper arms to stop flaring elbows; stay in Bridge.
Benefits: Energizes central nervous system; expands lungs; strengthens arms, wrists, legs, and spine.
Sequencing: Peak backbend of practice; requires thorough prep; follow with neutral supine poses before folds.
Prep Postures: Setu Bandha Sarvangasana, Ustrasana, Dolphin Pose.
What Needs to be Opened: Latissimus dorsi, subscapularis, pectorals, iliopsoas, rectus femoris.
What Needs to be Engaged: Triceps, serratus anterior, spinal erectors, glute max, quads.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Setu Bandha Sarvangasana; Dwi Pada Viparita Dandasana.
Common Misalignment: Feet turning out and splaying; elbows flaring wide; dumping into lumbar spine without shoulder opening.

Alignment: Tadasana foundation; arms swept overhead shoulder-width or palms pressed; biceps by ears; scapulae upwardly rotated.
Key Actions: Root feet down while reaching fingertips up; externally rotate upper arms; soften front ribs down.
Safety / Contraindications: Shoulder impingement, rotator cuff flare-ups, cervical strain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hands shoulder-width or in a "V"; hold strap between hands; gaze forward.
Benefits: Decompresses spine; stretches intercostals and axillary area; builds shoulder flexion.
Sequencing: Start of Surya Namaskar A & B; transitioning out of Tadasana.
Prep Postures: Tadasana, Gomukhasana arms prep, shoulder flossing.
What Needs to be Opened: Latissimus dorsi, pectoralis major/minor, subscapularis.
What Needs to be Engaged: Serratus anterior, triceps, quadriceps, deep core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Tadasana; Urdhva Vrikshasana, Utkatasana.
Common Misalignment: Flaring ribs and overarching lumbar spine; shrugging shoulders to ears.

Alignment: Hands stacked under shoulders, arms straight; tops of feet grounded; thighs, knees, hips floating completely off floor.
Key Actions: Press down through index knuckles; pull chest forward through upper arms; externally rotate arms; fire quads.
Safety / Contraindications: Wrist injuries, carpal tunnel, late pregnancy, acute low back pain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Substitute Cobra Pose; hands elevated on blocks to reduce wrist extension.
Benefits: Expands chest and lungs; strengthens wrists, triceps, spine; stretches psoas and abdominals.
Sequencing: Transition following Chaturanga and leading to Downward Dog in Surya Namaskar A & B.
Prep Postures: Bhujangasana, Setu Bandha Sarvangasana, High Plank.
What Needs to be Opened: Anterior chest, rectus abdominis, psoas major, anterior ankles.
What Needs to be Engaged: Triceps, serratus anterior (lower fibers), quads, back extensors.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Bhujangasana; Urdhva Dhanurasana, Matsyasana.
Common Misalignment: Dropping thighs/knees to floor; shrugging shoulders up to ears; hyperextending neck without chest lift.

Alignment: Front knee bent 90° over ankle; back foot angled out 45° with heel grounded; hips oriented forward.
Key Actions: Anchor outer back heel; scissor hips square; lengthen tailbone; lift chest and arms skyward.
Safety / Contraindications: SI joint instability, knee pain (medial collateral ligament), neck strain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Widen stance laterally (railroad tracks); lift back heel (High Lunge).
Benefits: Stretches hip flexors of trailing leg; strengthens quads, calves, glutes; builds ankle resilience.
Sequencing: Standing series in Surya Namaskar B; leads to Warrior 2, Humble Warrior, Warrior 3.
What Needs to be Opened: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris of back leg; back calf; thoracic spine.
What Needs to be Engaged: Front quad and hamstring; back gluteus maximus; core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Anjaneyasana; Virabhadrasana III, High Crescent Lunge.
Common Misalignment: Back heel lifting; back knee collapsing inward; over-arching lumbar spine.

Family / Category: External Standing / Hip Opening & Lateral Plane
Alignment: Stance 4–5 ft; front heel bisects back arch; front knee bent 90° over 2nd toe; torso vertical; arms parallel to floor.
Key Actions: Track front knee toward pinky toe; anchor outer back foot; lift pubic bone; gaze over front fingers.
Safety / Contraindications: Knee pathology (meniscus/MCL tears), hip impingement, neck strain.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Shorten stance; reduce front knee bend; hands on hips; back heel against wall.
Benefits: Opens adductors and hips; builds quad and shoulder endurance; stimulates pelvic circulation.
Sequencing: Foundational posture in lateral standing sequence; pairs with Side Angle, Triangle, Reverse Warrior.
What Needs to be Opened: Adductor magnus/longus (both legs), pectineus, groin, chest.
What Needs to be Engaged: Front quad and gluteus medius; external rotators; back abductors; deltoids.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Baddha Konasana; Utthita Parsvakonasana, Viparita Virabhadrasana.
Common Misalignment: Front knee collapsing inward (valgus); torso leaning forward over front thigh; back arch collapsing.

Alignment: Body in a horizontal "T" shape parallel to floor; standing leg vertical; lifted leg, spine, arms aligned.
Key Actions: Internally rotate back thigh (toes down); drive through back heel; lengthen crown forward; pull belly in.
Safety / Contraindications: Sacroiliac instability, low back injury, balance/vestibular issues.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hands on blocks under shoulders; arms back along hips (Airplane) or at heart center.
Benefits: Strengthens entire posterior chain; builds standing hip stability; conditions foot/ankle proprioceptors.
Sequencing: Late standing sequence; transitional hinge from High Lunge; leads to Half Moon or Standing Split.
Prep Postures: High Crescent Lunge, Ardha Uttanasana, Salabhasana.
What Needs to be Opened: Hamstrings and calves of standing leg.
What Needs to be Engaged: Standing glute medius; back leg glute max/hamstring; spinal erectors; core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Salabhasana; Ardha Chandrasana, Dekasana.
Common Misalignment: Lifted hip peeling open toward ceiling; sagging through lumbar spine; hyperextending knee.

Alignment: Seated with legs wide (90–120°); knees and toes point straight up; spine long as torso hinges from hip joints.
Key Actions: Root sit bones; actively flex feet and anchor heels; roll thighs back; walk hands forward with flat back.
Safety / Contraindications: Adductor strains, hamstring origin tears, lower back herniation.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Sit on folded blanket; hands behind hips to support upright spine; chest on bolster/blocks.
Benefits: Lengthens inner thighs and deep hamstrings; increases pelvic anterior mobility; opens pelvic floor.
Sequencing: Paired with Prasarita Padottanasana (seated version) or following Baddha Konasana.
Prep Postures: Prasarita Padottanasana, Baddha Konasana, Supta Padangusthasana B.
What Needs to be Opened: Adductor group, semimembranosus/semitendinosus, calves.
What Needs to be Engaged: Quadriceps, external hip rotators, erector spinae, core.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Prasarita Padottanasana (seated); Kurmasana.
Common Misalignment: Letting legs collapse forward inward; rounding through spine to touch floor.

Alignment: Feet wide (3.5–4.5 ft), outer edges parallel; hinge from hips; head hangs toward mat between feet.
Key Actions: Lift inner arches; pull inner thighs upward; rotate pelvis anteriorly; telescope torso downward.
Safety / Contraindications: Hamstring or adductor pulls, uncontrolled hypertension, vertigo.
Accessibility (Modifications / Variation: Hands or crown supported on blocks; soft knees; adjust stance width.
Benefits: Lengthens adductors and hamstrings; releases lower back; calms nervous system (inversion).
Sequencing: Mid-sequence standing transition; preparatory posture for Tripod Headstand.
What Needs to be Opened: Adductor group (inner thighs), hamstrings, plantar fascia.
What Needs to be Engaged: Quadriceps, anterior tibialis, gluteus medius.
Blueprint Pose & Related Postures / Vari: Uttanasana; Prasarita Padottanasana B, C, D.
Common Misalignment: Collapsing arches; shifting weight fully to heels; rounding spine instead of hinging.
